name: inkwash
summary: Traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour painting. Ink linework plus soft bleeding colour washes, full rendered environments, visible paper grain.
referenceNote: THE STYLE IS THE IMAGE. This plate — bongpot/outputs/flux2-probe/plate_00_reference.png, called 'the proven ink-wash man' and 'the loved ink-wash look' in nano-banana-test.mjs:8 — is what actually produced the results Ryan approves (reference/scene-counter.png, reference/scene-payphone.png, both rendered FROM it via nano-banana-pro image_input). Prompt text alone has never reproduced this. Always pass the reference; the prompt below is the secondary channel, not the definition.
prompt: Rendered in traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour painting style: confident dark ink-brush linework, loose expressive brushwork, soft bleeding colour washes, visible paper grain. Nothing photographic.
styleOnlyPrompt: Use the reference image ONLY as a painting-technique guide: copy its medium, brushwork, ink density, colour-wash behaviour and paper grain. Do NOT copy its subject, face, people, or composition. Paint a completely new picture showing: {SCENE}. Traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour painting: confident dark ink-brush linework, loose expressive brushwork, soft bleeding colour washes, visible paper grain. Nothing photographic.
referencePrompt: The same subject from the reference image — keep the exact face and identity — now {SCENE}. Rendered in the same traditional Chinese ink-and-watercolour painting style as the reference: confident dark ink-brush linework, loose expressive brushwork, soft bleeding colour washes, visible paper grain. Nothing photographic.
referencePromptNote: TWO DIFFERENT JOBS, do not confuse them. styleOnlyPrompt (the DEFAULT) borrows the medium and leaves the subject alone — for rendering new scenes in this style. referencePrompt (--identity) additionally locks the reference's face, which is what bongpot wanted when carrying ONE character across many shots; used by mistake it paints that man into every scene. Proven 2026-08-11: regenerating a Charlie Sheen ad shot with referencePrompt produced the plate's bald bearded man sitting in Sheen's car. The right long-term fix is a genuinely face-free swatch in reference/ — none exists yet; both bongpot 'swatches' are portraits.
platePrompt: Photographic character reference portrait, head to waist, three-quarter view facing camera, calm neutral resting expression. Plain seamless light-gray studio background, soft even diffuse light, no props, no scenery. Natural skin texture, documentary realism, not retouched.

notes.whatChanged2026-08-11: This file previously carried cutwork/config/creative.js:39 INK_WASH_STYLE verbatim. Live testing showed that string is WRONG for this look and actively harmful: it says 'near-monochromatic' and 'ink and bare cream paper dominate, generous negative space' — so restyling real footage DELETED the environment (a Sheen shot in a car came back floating on blank paper), and stills came out drained of the colour that defines the approved plates. It also ended in a negation clause ('no red seal stamp, no Chinese characters') that the same file documents as failing. The approved plates HAVE a red seal. Replaced with the short prompt from nano-banana-test.mjs that actually produced them.
notes.negationTrap: NEGATION DOES NOT WORK. Naming a forbidden thing summons it — the model weights the token, not the negation. Documented in creative.js:54-59 after flux-2-dev returned a wall of calligraphy plus a red seal from a prompt ending 'no red seal stamp, no Chinese characters'. The prompt above contains no negation except 'Nothing photographic', which is a positive medium statement.
notes.twoChannels: Content and style are separate inputs and must stay separate: the SCENE (what happens) comes from text — a shot description, e.g. from describe-video's shots.json; the LOOK comes from the reference image. This is the same decoupling creative.js:41-46 records for identity plates, and the USO graph (bongpot/tools/_uso.mjs) implements it a third way: identity plate + face-free style SWATCH through CLIPVision + content-only text, three channels, one graph.
notes.footageCaveat: For restyling REAL footage, do not add negative-space or bare-paper language — it instructs the model to erase the room. Keep the environment; change only the medium.

image.note: nano-banana-pro with image_input is the proven path for this style (33M runs, strongest identity coherence across reference angles). flux-2-dev via the VERSION endpoint also works but has not reproduced the plate look from text alone.

source: Style definition rebuilt 2026-08-11 from bongpot's proven artefacts, replacing the text-only extraction from cutwork/config/creative.js.
